theme_md_classic <- function() {
    theme_classic(
        base_size = 10, 
        base_family = "Helvetica",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text  = element_text(color = "black", size = 8),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}

## Consider test for overlaps

Idea is that the LFCs are generally not correlated and not related, but are 
there more than expected peaks that have high LFCs in both Glut & GABA?

I didn't see any issues with this code:

```{r}
get_region_pair <- function(dsres, region, use_shr = TRUE) {
    nm_g <- paste0(region, "_Glut")
    nm_b <- paste0(region, "_GABA")
    g <- dsres[[nm_g]]
    b <- dsres[[nm_b]]
    stopifnot(!is.null(g), !is.null(b))
    # join by peak id (rownames)
    common <- intersect(rownames(g), rownames(b))
    g <- g[common, , drop = FALSE]
    b <- b[common, , drop = FALSE]
    col_g <- if (use_shr) "log2FoldChange_shr" else "log2FoldChange"
    col_b <- if (use_shr) "log2FoldChange_shr" else "log2FoldChange"
    x <- g[[col_g]]
    y <- b[[col_b]]
    data.frame(peak = common, glut = x, gaba = y, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

joint_tail_test <- function(df, q = 0.95) {
    x <- df$glut
    y <- df$gaba
    tx <- quantile(x, q, na.rm = TRUE)
    ty <- quantile(y, q, na.rm = TRUE)
    hx <- x > tx
    hy <- y > ty
    
    ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
    hx <- hx[ok]; hy <- hy[ok]
    n  <- length(hx)
    
    n11 <- sum(hx & hy)
    n10 <- sum(hx & !hy)
    n01 <- sum(!hx & hy)
    n00 <- sum(!hx & !hy)
    
    # Fisher one-sided (enrichment in high-high cell)
    tab <- matrix(c(n11, n10, n01, n00), nrow = 2,
                  dimnames = list(Glut = c("High","Not"), GABA = c("High","Not")))
    ft  <- fisher.test(tab, alternative = "greater")
    
    # Binomial conditional test: P(GABA-high | Glut-high) > P(GABA-high)
    nA  <- n11 + n10
    pB  <- mean(hy)
    bt  <- if (nA > 0) binom.test(n11, nA, p = pB, alternative = "greater") else NULL
    
    data.frame(
        n = n,
        thresh_glut = tx,
        thresh_gaba = ty,
        n_glut_high = nA,
        n_gaba_high = n11 + n01,
        n_both_high = n11,
        expected_both = n * mean(hx) * mean(hy),
        fisher_odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate),
        fisher_p = ft$p.value,
        binom_p = if (is.null(bt)) NA_real_ else bt$p.value,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
}

run_all_regions <- function(dsres, regions, q = 0.95, use_shr = TRUE) {
    out <- lapply(regions, function(rg) {
        df <- get_region_pair(dsres, rg, use_shr = use_shr)
        ans <- joint_tail_test(df, q = q)
        cbind(region = rg, ans)
    })
    out <- do.call(rbind, out)
    # BH adjust across regions (do both p-values)
    out$fisher_p_adj <- p.adjust(out$fisher_p, method = "BH")
    out$binom_p_adj  <- p.adjust(out$binom_p, method = "BH")
    out <- out[order(out$fisher_p), ]
    rownames(out) <- NULL
    out
}
```

# All pairwise co-enrichments

Note this no longer specific to GABA vs. Glut.

I hate p-values, let's do something more comparative.

```{r}
# ----- All-pairs co-enrichment (upper tail only) -----
# dsres: named list of data.frames with rownames = peak ids
#        and columns including "log2FoldChange_shr" (or "log2FoldChange")
# q:     upper-tail quantile threshold (e.g., 0.95 or 0.99)
# use_shr: TRUE = use shrunken LFCs; FALSE = raw LFCs
#
# enrichment = observed_both / expected_both (under independence)
# pairs_upper: all pairwise combos ranked by enrichment (ties broken by n_both)
pairwise_coenrichment_upper <- function(dsres, q = 0.95, use_shr = TRUE) {
    nm <- names(dsres)
    region_of <- function(s) sub("_.*", "", s)
    nt_of     <- function(s) sub(".*_", "", s)
    col_lfc   <- if (use_shr) "log2FoldChange_shr" else "log2FoldChange"
    
    pairs <- t(combn(nm, 2))
    
    one_pair <- function(a, b) {
        da <- dsres[[a]]
        db <- dsres[[b]]
        common <- intersect(rownames(da), rownames(db))
        if (!length(common)) return(NULL)
        
        xa <- da[common, col_lfc]
        xb <- db[common, col_lfc]
        ok <- is.finite(xa) & is.finite(xb)
        xa <- xa[ok]; xb <- xb[ok]
        if (!length(xa)) return(NULL)
        
        ta <- quantile(xa, q, na.rm = TRUE)
        tb <- quantile(xb, q, na.rm = TRUE)
        ha <- xa > ta
        hb <- xb > tb
        
        n11 <- sum(ha & hb)
        pa  <- mean(ha); pb <- mean(hb)
        n   <- length(ha)
        exp_both <- n * pa * pb
        enrich   <- if (exp_both > 0) n11 / exp_both else NA_real_
        
        data.frame(
            A = a, B = b,
            region_A = region_of(a), nt_A = nt_of(a),
            region_B = region_of(b), nt_B = nt_of(b),
            same_region = region_of(a) == region_of(b),
            same_nt     = nt_of(a)     == nt_of(b),
            n = n, pA = pa, pB = pb,
            n_both = n11, expected_both = exp_both,
            enrichment = enrich,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    }
    
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) one_pair(pairs[i,1], pairs[i,2])))
    if (is.null(out) || !nrow(out)) 
        stop("No valid overlaps across pairs.")
    key <- out$enrichment; key[is.na(key)] <- -Inf
    o   <- order(key, out$n_both, decreasing = TRUE)
    out <- out[o, , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(out) <- NULL
    out$rank_overall <- seq_len(nrow(out))
    out
}
```

```{r}
# Upper-tail 99th percentile, using shrunken LFCs
all_pairs_coenr <- pairwise_coenrichment_upper(dsres, q = 0.99, use_shr = TRUE)
```

## Heatmap enrichments

```{r}
enr_mat <- matrix(
    NA, nrow=length(dsres), ncol=length(dsres),
    dimnames = list(names(dsres), names(dsres))
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(all_pairs_coenr))) {
    rw <- all_pairs_coenr$A[i]
    cl <- all_pairs_coenr$B[i]
    enr_mat[rw, cl] <- all_pairs_coenr$enrichment[i]
    enr_mat[cl, rw] <- all_pairs_coenr$enrichment[i]
}
```

```{r}
Heatmap(
    enr_mat, 
    heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "peak coenrichment\n(99th percentiles)\nobs/exp"),
    col = circlize::colorRamp2(c(0,20,40), c("#38598C", "white", "#B40426"))
)
```

```{r}
pdf(file.path(pdir, "heatmap_coenr_q99_of_lfcshr.pdf"), width=9)
Heatmap(
    enr_mat, 
    heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "peak coenrichment\n(99th percentiles)\nobs/exp"),
    col = circlize::colorRamp2(seq(0, 40, length.out=100), viridis::viridis(100))
)
invisible(dev.off())
```

log-enrichment:

```{r}
fix_inf <- function(x) {
    idx <- which(!is.finite(x), arr.ind = TRUE)
    x[idx] <- NA
    x
}
```

```{r}
range(log2(enr_mat) %>% .[!is.infinite(.)], na.rm=T)
```


```{r}
pdf(file.path(pdir, "heatmap_coenr_q99_of_lfcshr_log2.pdf"), width=9)
Heatmap(
    log2(enr_mat) %>% fix_inf, 
    heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "peak coenrichment\n(99th percentiles)\nlog2(obs/exp)"),
    col = circlize::colorRamp2(seq(-6, 6, length.out=100), viridis::viridis(100))
)
invisible(dev.off())

pdf(file.path(pdir, "heatmap_coenr_q99_of_lfcshr_log2_alt.pdf"), width=9)
Heatmap(
    log2(enr_mat) %>% fix_inf,

    col = circlize::colorRamp2(c(-6, 0, 6), c("blue", "white", "red"))
)
invisible(dev.off())
```

# Find some candidate peaks?

## HTH

The HTH peaks looked bad from the specificity score analysis, and yet we see
here the most co-enr of q99 peaks.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
    glut = dsres$HTH_Glut$log2FoldChange_shr,
    gaba = dsres$HTH_GABA$log2FoldChange_shr,
    row.names=rownames(dsres$HTH_Glut)
) %>% 
    mutate(
        comb = glut * gaba,
        rank_comb = rank(comb),
        rank_comb = length(rank_comb) - rank_comb
    )
```

```{r}
df[order(df$rank_comb), ] %>% 
    subset(glut>0 & gaba>0) %>% 
    head(20) %>% 
    print.data.frame
```
